bib.title: OPENCUA: Open Foundations for Computer-Use Agents
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2025 (39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)

question: How can an open framework (data collection tool, dataset, training recipe, models) build computer-use agents that approach proprietary ones?
hypothesis: Scaling CUA capability needs state-action pairs augmented with reflective long chain-of-thought reasoning, multi-image history and mixed data, rather than raw state-action pairs alone.
contributions: AgentNetTool: cross-OS annotation tool recording screen video, mouse/keyboard signals and accessibility trees
AgentNet: 22,625-task desktop trajectory dataset over Windows, macOS, Ubuntu
AgentNetBench: offline benchmark of 100 tasks with multiple gold actions per step
Training recipe: reflective long CoT synthesis, context encoding, data mixtures
OpenCUA models 7B/32B/72B plus A3B and Qwen2-7B variants, open-sourced

method.summary: Human demonstrations recorded with AgentNetTool are reduced to state-action pairs, augmented with synthesized L1/L2/L3 chain-of-thought (reflector, generator, summarizer built on claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219), and used for SFT of open VLMs (Qwen2-VL, Qwen2.5-VL, Kimi-VL-A3B) under three training strategies. Evaluated on OSWorld-Verified, WindowsAgentArena, AgentNetBench and four grounding benchmarks.
method.task: computer-use agent: screenshot plus instruction to PyAutoGUI action, supervised fine-tuning

datasets.name: AgentNet
datasets.size: 22,625 tasks (12K Windows, 5K macOS, 5K Ubuntu); 18.6 avg steps; 41,428 trajectories used for OpenCUA-7B/32B, 27,804 for Qwen2-7B and A3B
datasets.split: Win&Mac vs Ubuntu domain split; no overlap with OSWorld tasks
datasets.source: annotators on own computers; Moonshot AI annotated Ubuntu and released 5K trajectories
datasets.preprocessing: rule-based action reduction; keyframe state-action matching; reflective CoT synthesis; reflector drops incorrect or redundant steps

datasets.name: Grounding data (ShowUI, UGround, 189K AXTree bounding-box samples)
datasets.size: 189K parsed samples plus ShowUI and UGround (sizes not stated)

datasets.name: General SFT data (Kimi Team text and vision)
datasets.split: 35% general text in the main Qwen2 run; 30% general in Stage-2-only; 60% in joint training

datasets.name: AgentNetBench
datasets.size: 100 tasks, 2143 actions, 17.63 avg steps (61 Windows, 39 macOS)
datasets.source: selected near cluster centroids of AgentNet
datasets.preprocessing: manual review, multiple valid actions per step

other.note: classifies task domains and privacy sensitivity, rates complexity

models.name: Claude 4 Sonnet, Claude Sonnet 4.5, OpenAI CUA, Seed1.5-VL, UI-TARS-72B-DPO, Qwen3-VL, Qwen2.5-VL, Kimi-VL-A3B, Aguvis-7B

training.objective: supervised fine-tuning; loss on the assistant's final output (CoT + action)
training.lr: Stage-2-only (Qwen2-7B, A3B): 2e-5; 32B Stage 1: 3e-5, Stage 2: 2.5e-5; 72B Stage 1: 2.5e-5 decaying to 1.5e-5, Stage 2: 1.5e-5 decaying to 2e-6; 7B joint: peak 2.5e-5, min 3e-6
training.lr_schedule: decay as stated per stage (shape not named)
training.warmup: 400-step grounding warm-up for OpenCUA-Qwen2-7B (a data stage, not an LR warmup); LR warmup not stated
training.batch_size: Qwen2-7B/A3B: 384 (512 in ablations); 32B Stage 1: 3,584, Stage 2: 512; 72B Stage 1: 600, Stage 2: batch size not stated; 7B: 512
training.steps: Qwen2-7B 3,400 steps after 400 warm-up steps; A3B 2,000 steps; 32B Stage 2 final step 4,700; 7B best checkpoint step 14,600
training.epochs: 3 epochs for multi-image trajectory samples in joint training
training.seq_len: 32,768 (Qwen2-7B and A3B); not stated for others
training.weight_decay: 0.1 (Qwen2-7B and A3B); not stated for others
training.hardware: A100 GPUs: 96 (Qwen2-7B, A3B), 224 (32B Stage 1), 128 (32B Stage 2), 480 (72B stages), 128 (7B)
training.wall_clock: Qwen2-7B about 45 h; A3B about 10 h; OpenCUA-7B eight days

other.framework: Kimi Team infrastructure with Megatron and DeepSpeed ZeRO-3
other.mixes: Stage-2-only 70% CUA (planning:grounding 4:1) + 30% general; 32B Stage 2 45% planning, 20% grounding, rest general; 7B joint 20/20/60 planning/grounding/general
other.position_encoding: 1D RoPE instead of M-RoPE; Kimi-VL chat template and tokenizer used for all
other.trajectory_counts: Qwen2-7B/A3B 18k Win&macOS + 10k Ubuntu; 32B and 7B 18k Win&macOS + 20k Ubuntu
other.visual_history: 3 screenshots default; history text uses L1 CoT
other.max_pixels: 12,845,056 for Qwen2.5-VL vs 829,440 for Qwen2-VL and Kimi-VL-A3B
other.72B Stage 2 lr and batch: text prints 'batch size, LR 1.5e-5 decay to 2e-6' with the batch size missing
other.appendix_F_case: Chrome extension install task, 15 steps; agent detours via Web Store sign-in at steps 4-6, backs out at step 6, then reaches Developer mode, Load unpacked, Desktop helloExtension, and terminates success at step 15; actions use relative coordinates e.g. pyautogui.click(x=0.988, y=0.081)

inference.samples: OSWorld-Verified average of 3 runs; Pass@3 = best of 3 runs; Pass@16 study with 16 runs at temp 0.1 on OpenCUA-Qwen2-7B
inference.prompting: L2 CoT format (Thought + Action) at inference; system prompt specifies Thought/Action format and PyAutoGUI output (App G)

metrics.name: OSWorld-Verified success rate
metrics.definition: fraction of tasks passing the per-task script within the step budget, mean of 3 runs

metrics.name: Pass@n
metrics.definition: success in at least one of n runs

metrics.name: AgentNetBench Step SR
metrics.definition: per-step action correctness: bounding-box hit for coordinate actions, edit distance for write, exact match for hotkey/press, correct step for terminate

eval.protocol: OSWorld-Verified results from the public evaluation by the OSWorld team on AWS; 3 runs, spread shown as +/- in Table 3; no significance test; ablations single run

availability.data: annotation tool, datasets released; Moonshot AI releases 5K Ubuntu trajectories

prompts.purpose: L1 system prompt (Action only); loss on assistant output
prompts.text: You are a GUI agent. You are given a task and a screenshot of the screen. You need to perform a series of pyautogui actions to complete the task. For each step, provide your response in this format: Action: Provide clear, concise, and actionable instructions: - If the action involves interacting with a specific target: - Describe target explicitly without using coordinates - Specify element names when possible (use original language if non-English) - Describe features (shape, color, position) if name unavailable - For window control buttons, identify correctly (minimize, maximize, close) - if the action involves keyboard actions like 'press', 'write', 'hotkey': - Consolidate repetitive keypresses with count - Specify expected text outcome for typing actions. Finally, output the action as PyAutoGUI code or the following functions: (function schemas for computer.triple_click(x,y) and computer.terminate(status: success|failure))
prompts.where: App G.1 (reconstructed from spaced extraction; function list truncated to two schemas as printed)

prompts.text: ... format: Thought: - Step by Step Progress Assessment: - Analyze completed task parts and their contribution to the overall goal - Reflect on potential errors, unexpected results, or obstacles - If previous action was incorrect, predict a logical recovery step - Next Action Analysis: - List possible next actions based on current state - Evaluate options considering current state and previous actions - Propose most logical next action - Anticipate consequences of the proposed action - For Text Input Actions: - Note current cursor position - Consolidate repetitive actions (specify count for multiple keypresses) - Describe expected final text outcome - Use first-person perspective in reasoning. Action: (as L1)

... format: Observation: - Describe the current computer state based on the full screenshot in detail. - Application Context: - The active application - The active window or page - Overall layout and visible interface - Key Elements: - Menu items and toolbars - Buttons and controls - Text fields and content - Dialog boxes or popups - Error messages or notifications - Loading states - Other key elements - Describe any content, elements, options, information or clues that are possibly relevant to achieving the task goal, including their name, content, or shape (if possible). Thought: (as L2) Action: (as L1)
# Task Instruction: <task> Please generate the next move according to the screenshot, task instruction and previous steps (if provided).

Multi-turn dialogue: earlier steps appear as assistant turns with L1 '# Step n: ## Action:...' (history uses L1 only) interleaved with user turns holding screenshots; only the last assistant turn (Step 5 in the example, '## Code: pyautogui.click(x=0.157, y=0.1229)') carries the full CoT and enters the loss. Coordinates are relative (0-1).

limits: Dataset scale is limited by human annotation effort; annotators may not use the most efficient method (shortcuts, scripts) (App A)
Informed consent introduces selection bias (App A)
Models struggle with error recognition, repetitive loops, termination, precision grounding and long-horizon tasks (Sec 4.2, App E)
Online benchmarks have large variance; Pass@n gaps show instability even at temperature 0 (Sec 5)
Ablations are single-run with small-model (7B Qwen2-VL) settings; steps for the reflective-CoT ablation are not stated
Table 11 72B row is labelled PREVIEW while Table 3 reports it as OpenCUA-72B
Results concern OSWorld-Verified at snapshot of Oct 2025; proprietary leaders have moved
